title: Tailor Your CV to a Specific Role
summary: Change emphasis for a vacancy while keeping your experience accurate and consistent.
learningObjectives: Review AI edits for factual changes.
Keep a record of the submitted version.

sections.heading: Tailoring starts with the job, not with synonyms
body: Tailoring means helping a reader see the relevant parts of your existing experience. It does not mean rewriting your history to match every requirement. Begin with one verified job description and your master CV. Extract the three or four responsibilities that appear central to the role. Keep practical conditions, essential technical requirements and preferences distinct.

Imagine a role focused on Apex integrations and LWC maintenance. Your master CV contains a test-drive form, a mock callout exercise and unrelated earlier software work. The form and callout deserve more space than an unrelated visual design experiment. You still need to label the callout as a training exercise if that is what it was.

callouts.text: Tailoring changes selection, order and explanation. It should not change the facts.

sections.heading: Map each priority to the strongest available evidence
body: Create a small table: employer responsibility, your evidence, CV location and unresolved gap. For “maintain LWC,” point to a component where you can explain data flow, loading and error states. For “support production integrations,” a mock exercise is partial preparation, not proof that you have owned production incidents. Keep that gap visible in your preparation notes.

Prefer an exact technical term when it accurately describes your work. If you used Queueable Apex, name it instead of saying only “background work.” Do not insert a technology merely because the description contains it. A keyword without a supporting example can create an interview question that exposes the mismatch.

sections.heading: Use AI as an editor with a boundary
body: An assistant can compare two supplied documents and propose clearer wording. Tell it to preserve employers, dates, ownership, technologies and measurements. Ask for changes with reasons so that you can review them. If it suggests a new accomplishment, reject the suggestion unless you have independent evidence for it.

Review the output line by line against the master CV. Pay particular attention to subtle upgrades: “practised” becoming “led,” “training org” disappearing, or “supported a developer” becoming “architected the solution.” These changes may sound polished but alter the meaning. The final file is your representation of your experience, so you must understand and approve every claim.

callouts.text: A more confident verb can change a factual claim. Check ownership and context, not just spelling.

codeBlocks.caption: Reusable working prompt or template
codeBlocks.code:
Compare this job description with my master CV.
Identify the three most relevant responsibilities and the existing evidence for each.
Suggest edits to emphasis and clarity only.
Do not add employers, dates, technologies, metrics, credentials or responsibilities.
Keep training projects labelled as training.
For each proposed edit, explain the reason and quote the evidence it uses.
List unsupported requirements separately as preparation gaps.

sections.heading: Save a version you can reconstruct
body: Save the tailored CV with the employer, role and date in your private application records. Record the source job description and the actual submitted file. You may later need to explain a project that was highlighted in that version. Keeping the file prevents confusion between several similar applications.

Finish with a consistency check: dates match the master, links work, the summary fits the role and no essential context has vanished. Then decide whether the application is worthwhile given the remaining gaps. A tailored CV can make a real match clearer; it cannot create experience that you do not yet have.

callouts.text: For each changed bullet, identify the original evidence and explain why this employer is likely to care about it.

exercise.title: Apply this to your own search
exercise.brief: Tailor your master CV to one verified vacancy and keep a change log.
steps: Map each to evidence and identify gaps.
Reorder or clarify the relevant sections.
Review every proposed AI edit if you use an assistant.
Save the final version with the job description and a short change log.
acceptance: Every claim remains consistent with the master CV.
The most relevant evidence is prominent.
Unsupported requirements are recorded as gaps rather than disguised as experience.

knowledgeCheck.question: What should change when tailoring a CV?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Selection, order and wording of relevant evidence, while the facts remain consistent.

knowledgeCheck.question: Should all missing keywords be inserted?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. Use a term only if it accurately describes experience you can explain.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why keep the submitted version?
knowledgeCheck.answer: It lets you prepare for the exact examples and claims the interviewer has read.

recap: Review AI edits for factual changes.
Keep a record of the submitted version.
